Arkansas State just dropped to 4-6 after a loss to Coastal Carolina

        Arkansas State has fired Butch Jones amidst his sixth season with the program, according to 247Sports. There's a chance that Jones could coach the last two games of the season, according to ESPN, but no decision has been made at this time.Entering November, Arkansas State was 4-4 with what appeared to be a manageable schedule ahead. Then, the Red Wolves dropped two winnable games to UL-Monroe and Coastal Carolina. That was the final straw for Jones, whose teams have gotten progressively worse over the last few seasons.Arkansas State hired Jones in 2021, and the team steadily improved in each of his first four seasons on the job — reaching bowl eligibility three times over that span. The Red Wolves' performance under Jones peaked with an eight-win season in 2024, but it has dipped in each subsequent year. Jones exits Jonesboro with an overall record of 30-43.
Jones began his coaching career as an offensive assistant and worked his way up the ladder at Central Michigan until he took over the program in 2007. After three successful seasons and two conference titles with the Chippewas, Jones made the jump to Cincinnati, where he won a pair of Big East championships.In 2013, Jones got an opportunity to coach at a major program when Tennessee hired him. He posted back-to-back nine-win seasons with the Vols in 2015 and 2016, but the team cratered in 2017, which led to his firing.
Jones then spent three seasons working as an offensive analyst for Nick Saban at Alabama before landing at Arkansas State. In 17 years as a coach, Jones has compiled an overall record of 114-97.

        All we heard for much of this season was that the Kansas City Chiefs had taken on a new offensive persona. They were now a running team with Kenneth Walker.Yeah, sure.Yes, they have leaned on the running game for the early part of the season, in large part because of a lack of quality receivers, the addition of Walker and quarterback Patrick Mahomes recovering from a torn ACL in 2025. But Sunday's blowout victory over the Atlanta Falcons reminded us that this team will go only as far as the right arm of Mahomes, who looked all the way back from the ACL injury Sunday and overcame an elbow injury suffered last week.With Walker missing the Falcons game because of a groin injury, all Mahomes did was throw for 348 yards and five touchdowns to remind the doubters that he is much more than a game manager who just turns and hands the ball off.Walker has been mentioned as an MVP candidate. Reminder: He isn't even the MVP on his own team. Mahomes is that.
The addition of receiver Josh Downs at the trade deadline helps give Mahomes more weapons. Downs had a touchdown Sunday, as did rookie speedster Cyrus Allen, who may be on the verge of breaking out.The backfield was also in good hands with rookie running back Emmett Johnson, who scored two touchdowns and accounted for 171 total yards, rushing for 101. He was able to replace Walker easily, but that injury largely forced the Falcons to turn back to Mahomes of old.The 7-2 Chiefs are still sixth in my Power Rankings this week, but as that passing game gets back to what we've come to see in other years from Mahomes, they will be a real Super Bowl threat.
When Walker comes back, they can run it with anybody. With Mahomes under center, they can throw it with anybody — especially with the receiver group improving.The defense is ranked third in scoring, giving up just 17.3 points per game. They are eighth in total defense and tied for sixth in yards allowed per play.Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has this young group playing good defense.The Chiefs are back. Mostly, though, Mahomes is back, which is why they are a real threat in the AFC to go to the Super Bowl. You want to go to Arrowhead to play them in the playoffs with that guy? Didn't think so.

body:
Widely considered the best player in high school basketball, Daughtry burst on the national scene with an absurd 2026 Peach Jam showing to cap off a rocketship summer on the Nike EYBL circuit

        The biggest and baddest name in high school basketball is off the board. Cayden Daughtry, a dynamic 6-foot point guard who re-wrote the Peach Jam record books, has committed to John Calipari and Arkansas in a bombshell, late-Monday evening decision. Daughtry is the No. 3-ranked player in the Class of 2027, per 247Sports. He picked Arkansas over Florida State in a recruitment that evolved greatly in the final hours. Miami and Florida were once considered the top dawgs in the race for the electric PG1, but both exited from the race on Monday. Recruiting in 2026 has evolved into the two-headed monster of evaluation and negotiation. Period. The evaluation question for Daughtry became very easy after a rocket-ship summer on the Nike EYBL circuit. The negotiation? That was quite a different story. Daughtry's deal with Arkansas will be in the $4 million neighborhood, sources told CBS Sports. Depth Chart 101 is another reason why Miami and Florida held off from meeting the asking price for Daughtry. Florida is expected to retain starting point guard Boogie Fland and top sharpshooter Urban Klavzar, the reigning SEC Sixth Man of the Year. Miami hopes to get dynamic point guard Acaden Lewis back for a second season in Coral Gables. So a recruitment that seemed destined to end with Daughtry, a Fort Lauderdale native, landing with an in-state school had a late-night twist, opening the door for John Calipari to add yet another five-star guard to his record-breaking resume. 

        
            
                College basketball picks, schedule: Predictions for Duke vs. Illinois and more Top 25 games on Tuesday
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
While his NBA appeal is still a debate in some circles, there's no question who the most productive player in high school basketball is at this very moment. Daughtry's stock catapulted this summer and crested when he led his Florida Rebels club to the 17U Peach Jam championship. The 6-foot, 165-pound point guard averaged a mind-blowing 32.3 points, 6.1 assists, 4.9 rebounds and 2.9 steals with elite efficiency. Daughtry shot 63% on 2s, 49% from 3-point range and 91% from the charity stripe over a grueling eight games in five days gauntlet. Peach Jam has been around for 30 years, and Daughtry's fireball week had the gym in North Augusta buzzing for weeks."Trae Young," Florida Rebels coach Steve Reece says when asked about Daughtry's best comparison. "I mean, he shoots deep. Trae Young here at this level was special. They both nasty on the court."
        
            
                SEC abides by court order in RJ Luis eligibility saga: LSU is now free to add ex-St. John's star
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Peach Jam eliminated all questions about the detractors around his size. The NBA is a grown-man league, and Daughtry is small and thin. Daughtry measured a shade under 6 feet tall barefoot, with a wingspan hovering around 6-foot-3. There are only five current NBA players in that zip code, size-wise: Young, Jose Alvarado, Fred VanVleet, Jamal Shead and TJ McConnell.
"I mean, there's no getting past it," Daughtry told CBS Sports in July at Peach Jam. "It's true. Just gotta come in and just keep playing. Obviously, it's gonna be a thing for my whole life, so just gotta hear it, let it go out one ear, out the other, and just keep playing."Then, the games start, and the hesitations quickly disappear. Daughtry has a wizard handle, a lightning-quick first step and a feathery jumper. His pull-up jumper is automatic. He's dripping in dawg, too. Daughtry walks onto every floor, just itching to kill. Daughtry's competitive spirit is one of the most attractive parts of his game. Now, he's off to Arkansas to replace eventual lottery pick Jordan Smith Jr., who replaced eventual lottery pick Darius Acuff and on and on we go.
Get your popcorn ready.

        Five-star combo guard Adan Diggs committed to Arizona on CBS Sports HQ on Monday evening. The No. 6 overall player in the 2027 recruiting cycle by 247Sports marks the first member of the Wildcats' upcoming recruiting class.The Goodyear, Ariz., product committed to the Wildcats over Arkansas, Kentucky and USC. Diggs is the second-highest-ranked player from the 2027 recruiting cycle to pledge his college commitment. Last month, DeMarcus Henry — the No. 4 overall player in the class — committed to North Carolina. 
Other players from the 2027 recruiting class who recently committed include five-star center Lewis Uvwo (Providence), five-star guard Reese Alston (LSU), five-star forward Jordan Page (UConn) and four-star forward Asa Montgomery (Duke).Diggs is just the latest five-star that coach Tommy Lloyd has landed since arriving at Arizona in 2021, joining Caleb Holt (2026), Koa Peat (2025) and Brayden Burries (2025). 247Sports Director of Scouting Adam Finklestein says that Arizona is getting "one of the more naturally gifted two-way prospects in the national class."
"Physically, he has solid size for a combo-guard, good length (6-foot-7 wingspan), and an emerging power body. He's a good, not great, vertical athlete, who is better when he can elevate off two, and also a fluid mover. He's a very talented defender, both on and off the ball. He has some versatility, but can also impact the game around the rim. He's athletic and competitive on the glass (6.1 per game in EYBL) and capable of being the weakside low-man and even challenging plays at the rim."Arizona finished with the second-best recruiting class in 2025 and ranked No. 13 last cycle (2026) in the 247Sports rankings. With a commitment from Diggs, Arizona is on track to finish with one of the top classes in the 2027 recruiting cycle.

        Welcome to the Week 10 grades!It was a day of statement wins around the NFL and the biggest statement was made by the Minnesota Vikings. In their first game since trading for Kirk Cousins, the Vikings pounded the Packers 30-10, and the impressive part is that they did that at Lambeau Field. Combined with their 39-22 win in Week 1, they became the first team since 1987 to beat the Packers by at least 17 points twice in a season. Patrick Mahomes also made a statement on Sunday and that's the Chiefs offense can still function just fine without Kenneth Walker. In Kansas City's 35-13 win over Atlanta, Mahomes threw five TD passes in a game for the first time since 2022. He also threw for 348 yards, and a big reason was that he finally had the long ball working. Mahomes, who had gone 20 straight games without throwing a touchdown pass that traveled at least 20 yards in the air, produced two of those against the Falcons. Deshaun Watson also made a statement. The Browns quarterback led ANOTHER fourth-quarter comeback and just became only the third QB in NFL history with a game-winning drive in each of his team's first six wins in a season (1990 Troy Aikman and 2016 Matthew Stafford). 
And then there was Joe Burrow. The Bengals QB made a statement on Sunday night against the Steelers with four touchdown passes in a dominating 38-18 win. Burrow now has at least four total touchdowns in five straight games, which is tied with Peyton Manning (2004) for the longest streak in NFL history. On Monday night, the Chargers made a statement by winning their first game of the season. They shot out to a 10-0 lead and then held on for dear life. And now, let's get to the Week 10 grades, starting with the Chargers' surprising win.

title: Ravens vs. Chargers prediction: Can L.A. get its first win on 'MNF' against the injury-plagued Ravens? - CBS Sports
description: Plus, how to watch, odds, a preview and a prediction for the Monday night matchup
body:
Plus, how to watch, odds, a preview and a prediction for the Monday night matchup
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers. Baltimore is coming off a disastrous Thursday night loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, during which the offense looked inept with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center while nursing an injury. The Ravens will now turn to the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett in hopes that he can reinvigorate the attack in the absence of both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball. The Chargers are once again beset by a cavalcade of injuries, but that is no excuse for just how poorly they have played. They're the only winless team in the league at the moment, so they'll be looking for their first victory of the season.Will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.Where to watch Ravens vs. Chargers liveDate: Monday, Nov. 16 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore)TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Ravens -4.5, O/U 38.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Chargers have the ballThe Chargers are 26th in the NFL in total yards and 32nd (a.k.a., last) in points. They average a mere 4.7 yards per play, which is 29th in the league, and they have scored points on only 27.4% of their drives while turning it over a league-worst 18.9% of the time. They lead the NFL in pre-snap penalties per game. They don't do anything well, and they often put themselves behind the eight ball with inexcusable mistakes. 
Justin Herbert looks like a broken quarterback, completing just 61.3% of his passes at an average of 6.8 yards per attempt, with six touchdown passes against a league-worst 11 interceptions. His receiver corps has been brutal all season, dropping passes and seemingly miscommunicating with him on routes left and right. He once again won't have Ladd McConkey on Monday evening, either, which will leave the uninspiring trio of Quentin Johnston, Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith as his top perimeter options.Los Angeles has been entirely unable to run the ball, with Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combining for 709 yards on 184 carries -- an average of 3.8 yards per tote. The offensive line has given them no room to run whatsoever, clearing the way for only 0.90 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media. The backs themselves have a slightly below-average avoided tackle rate, but they still check in considerably below average in yards after contact per carry.Other than all that, though, things are going really well!That said, the Ravens do provide the Chargers with an opportunity to at least move the ball. Baltimore is 25th in the league in scoring defense and 21st in yards allowed per play. The Ravens have shown themselves to be beatable mostly through the air, as they've allowed only 3.6 yards per carry this season. Herbert doesn't have his top receiving option available in this game, but if the offensive line can actually provide him with adequate time to throw (not a guarantee with this group, obviously), then perhaps he can throw the ball to the guys wearing his color shirts rather than the opposing team for a change.
When the Ravens have the ballIt's hard to know what to expect from Baltimore's offense given that the Ravens are now on their fourth starting quarterback. This time around, it is the one who has yet to play with his new team and arrived in town just a week and a half ago. We know that Brissett has completed 63.3% of his passes for only 5.6 yards per attempt this season, with 10 touchdowns against seven interceptions. We also know that he was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew before being traded from Arizona to Baltimore. He's competent and can keep the offense moving at times, but he doesn't offer much in terms of ceiling.We also know that Brissett likes to hyper-target his top options in the passing game. We saw that in Arizona with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, but we also saw it in other stops, like when he honed in on Amari Cooper during his year as the starter with the Cleveland Browns. The Ravens already focus the majority of their passing game on wide receiver Zay Flowers, and it wouldn't be surprising if Brissett peppered him with targets here. 
Flowers was having a monster season with Lamar Jackson and even Tyler Huntley under center, but he did nothing the last two weeks with Joe Fagnano in the lineup, essentially. He should get back to producing at a decent level here, provided that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle moves him around the formation rather than parking him in the slot, where the Chargers have been better in coverage than they have been on the outside. Still, the Ravens will likely look to center the offense on Derrick Henry, so that Brissett doesn't have to do a ton of heavy lifting. Henry hasn't been as efficient this season (3.9 yards per carry) as he was during his first two years with the Ravens (5.6 per carry), presumably in part because he hasn't had Jackson to draw defensive attention away from his runs up the middle. Henry does still have a 53.7% rushing success rate, but he hasn't broken the types of long runs we've been used to seeing from him because the wider rushing lanes are not available with defenses crowding the box. He's run into an eight-man box on 30.9% of his carries, according to Tru Media, the third-highest rate among the 26 players with at least 100 rushing attempts so far this season.
The Chargers have actually been half-way decent against the run this year, allowing 4.1 yards per carry to opposing running backs, but they've been hit for explosives at an above-average rate. If they don't get Henry on the ground quickly, he could hit a crease and take it a long way. If that starts happening, it'll open things up for Brissett to work the play-action game, which could lead to big plays for the likes of Flowers, Ja'Kobi Lane and perhaps even Mark Andrews.PredictionI don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. title: Mauricio Pochettino's final go with USMNT is all about pivoting to the future before Manchester United move - CBS Sports
description: Pochettino will coach his final game with the USMNT on Tuesday, the second leg of the Concacaf Nations League qua
body:
Pochettino will coach his final game with the USMNT on Tuesday, the second leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti, before joining Manchester United later in the week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:02 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Three days after tearing up as he announced his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.After two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time."For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that says it's not important tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform."How to watch USMNT vs. Haiti, oddsDate: Tuesday, Nov. 17 | Time: 7 p.m. ETLocation: TQL Stadium -- CincinnatiTV: TNT | Live stream: HBO MaxOdds: USMNT -2000; Draw +1100; Haiti +1500Pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his plans for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.
"What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the new coaches that arrive here," Pochettino said. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow."For all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.For perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an important new chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.
Pochettino set to begin Manchester United pivotAs for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his new role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.Two years removed from starting a new job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-important clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return."For me, it's not difficult," he said of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most important [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow."
A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are currently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

title: Sean Payton disputes Jim Harbaugh's 'loophole' claim after Broncos-Chargers trade falls apart - CBS Sports
description: The Broncos coach rejected Harbaugh's criticism of the process that derailed Denver's trade for Chargers lineback
body:
The Broncos coach rejected Harbaugh's criticism of the process that derailed Denver's trade for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        At the trade deadline last Tuesday, a rare inter-division deal was agreed to between the Los Angeles Chargers and Denver Broncos. The Broncos agreed to send the Chargers a fourth-round pick and a future fifth-round pick in exchange for linebacker Daiyan Henley, but the deal fell apart.The trade was nixed after Denver reportedly found an issue with Henley's knee during his physical. ESPN reported that the Broncos then approached the Chargers and attempted to renegotiate the compensation. Denver still wanted to acquire the linebacker, but just not at the price George Paton and Sean Payton initially agreed to.Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that the Broncos backing out of the deal sets a bad precedent, and that this is a "loophole" the NFL needs to investigate."That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that," Harbaugh said. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass/fail for a medical trade. They told us they weren't going to pass him if there was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. They would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a 'fill in the blank.' I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."The Broncos were on a bye in Week 10, so we had to wait until Monday to hear their side of the story. Payton was indeed asked about the trade falling through, but didn't offer many details. 
"I'm not going to get into the specifics. He's prospect we thought of — and still do — very highly of. It just didn't work out," Payton said, via The Athletic. "I'll leave it at that."What did Payton think about Harbaugh's comments regarding a "loophole?"  "Listen, I thought I saw it all," he said, via Mile High Sports. "There's no loophole. It's just part of the trade process, every step of the way." 
Whatever the Broncos found in Henley's knee hasn't affected him yet. He hasn't missed a game due to injury in each of the last two seasons. In eight games played this season, Henley has recorded 51 tackles, half a sack, two passes defensed and an interception. The Broncos and Chargers will see each other again in the regular-season finale when Week 18 rolls around.

title: Looking at Rory McIlroy's two-act career and PGA Tour cards being exchanged - CBS Sports
description: The weekend in golf is not quite over yet, but the Monday Tee Sheet has plenty to cover
body:
The weekend in golf is not quite over yet, but the Monday Tee Sheet has plenty to cover
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:23 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Rory McIlroy's career has been analyzed, picked apart, applauded and criticized, yet even as he traverses into his late 30s, he continues to draw the attention of golf fans. This past weekend, McIlroy won his eighth Race to Dubai crown (fifth in a row), pulling him alongside Colin Montgomerie for the most all-time on the European circuit.There is little doubt what McIlroy can do on the golf course, especially considering how long he has been doing it. After all, he has been ranked inside the top 20 of the Official World Golf Rankings since October 2009. Let's restate that for dramatic purposes: McIlroy has been ranked inside the top 20 of the OWGR since October 2009. The top three players in the world at the time? Tiger Woods, Phil Mickelson and Steve Stricker. There is a common misconception in golf circles that longevity is not often appreciated or celebrated. The pendulum has largely swung too far in one direction on that ill-conceived talking point.
McIlroy has been the man for nearly two decades. Adam Scott, Justin Rose and many others have enjoyed long, successful careers and continue to put their best foot forward even into their 40s. This is the way the game is trending. Competitive players will emerge from their 20s, 30s, and yes, even their 40s. Heck, last week there was one still in his teens.What is so compelling about McIlroy's arc, though, is not the consistency he has been able to blanket across his career. Rather, it is the windows in which he has summited the proverbial mountaintop and the number of times he has done so.Let's have his Race to Dubai titles do the hard work for us to identify those periods. 
Rory McIlroy's Race to Dubai victoriesYearWinnerRunner-up2026Rory McIlroyEugenio Chacarra2025Rory McIlroyMarco Penge2024Rory McIlroyRasmus Højgaard2023Rory McIlroyNicolai Højgaard2022Rory McIlroyRyan Fox2015Rory McIlroyDanny Willett2014Rory McIlroyHenrik Stenson2012Rory McIlroyJustin RoseFrom 2012-16, McIlroy claimed 17 worldwide victories consisting of three major championships, two World Golf Championships, two DP World Tour Championships, the Tour Championship, the BMW PGA Championship and the Irish Open. In that span, he claimed a FedEx Cup and three Race to Dubai crowns.A decade later, he has accomplished something similar. From 2022-26, he had 15 worldwide wins, including two Masters, The Players Championship, the DP World Tour Championship, the Tour Championship, the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am and the Irish Open. In that span, he claimed a FedEx Cup and five Race to Dubai crowns.Careers are made in pockets of greatness stretching anywhere from two to five years. It happens all the time in golf. What doesn't, though, is a second act like that being enjoyed by McIlroy, one equal in accomplishments but greater in grit.It's just rare. For as much as experience can lift players past newcomers, there comes a time when it starts to weigh them down just as equally.The decade-long major drought, the agonizing close calls and noise that followed him outside the ropes. It's buried stars before him and will bury those after him. But McIlroy managed, and he used it as fuel for a second act that rivals his first, proving that his real superpower isn't just how high his floor is, but how many times he's been able to reach his ceiling.Welcome to the showLadies and gentlemen, welcome your class of 2026 DP World Tour graduates! These 10 men have all found new jobs on the PGA Tour for next year, except for ... wait a minute ... that guy looks familiar! Didn't he ... already?! Oh well, these players will all come stateside in 2027, including America's own Patrick Reed.That's right, he's back!
Reed's name may lead the way, but in terms of points, that honor goes to Eugenio Chacarra, who nearly won the Race to Dubai. Chacarra will be a fun one to watch next season and beyond as the 26-year-old Spaniard has an old-school energy and look to his game. Reed and Chacarra have enough game to contend, compete and keep up with the players on the PGA Tour, but that has not always been the case since the DP World Tour started sending over its top 10 finishers, who were not otherwise exempt, from the Race to Dubai.This current season has been the best effort since its inception with Kristoffer Reitan, Alex Noren and Jordan Smith all keeping their cards as John Parry and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen have a chance to as well in the last week of the PGA Tour season.DP World Tour graduatesEugenio ChacarraPatrick ReedCasey JarvisJayden SchaperDaniel HillierJacob Skov OlesenOliver LindellAndy SullivanBernd WiesbergerJoe DeanSpeaking of …The 2026 PGA Tour season comes to an end this week at the RSM Classic once they finish the Austin Championship, which continues to be a complete nightmare for the Tour. The Tour chose to cancel play on Sunday due to rain and will wrap up the tournament on Monday before heading to Sea Island, Georgia, which is one of my favorite places on Earth.I've always found it to be such a funny juxtaposition -- Sea Island and the stakes at hand. An easygoing, laid-back community welcomes the Tour into town for a week, during which some jobs will be secured, and others will be lost. It will also be a clash of eras, as the young guns are the main attraction for those on-site looking to watch golf. Michael Brennan, Jackson Koivun, Blades Brown and Ben James headline the field with Billy Horschel, Chandler Phillips, Chris Kirk and Lee Hodges flirting with the top-100 cutoff.

title: Lane Kiffin relives LSU's 'nightmare' finish in loss to Texas - CBS Sports
description: The LSU coach regretted not calling a timeout before Arch Manning's game-winning touchdown
body:
The LSU coach regretted not calling a timeout before Arch Manning's game-winning touchdown
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Saturday night's gut-wrenching loss to Texas is still haunting Lane Kiffin -- literally and figuratively. The LSU coach hasn't yet processed the sight of Raleek Brown walking into the end zone untouched on Arch Manning's game-winning touchdown pass.A season that began with a lot of hype, optimism and financial investment has resulted in a 6-4 record through 10 games. Few coaches have faced as much pressure in Year 1 as Kiffin, and he felt that weight as Brown went uncovered for the game-winning touchdown."Not in a negative way," Kiffin said Monday. "I think we all know here that LSU football wins and losses mean so much to everyone in the state. You do feel that."I had a moment when that ball went in, and my immediate thought was for our players. They put in all this work, did all this in the offseason, and all these guys came here. I was just thinking, "It's going to come down to this? We're not going to f---ing cover the guy, and he's going to walk into the f---ing end zone.
"Then our fans, after all the energy in the game, had it right there to win, and that's what it comes down to. I felt it, but not in a bad way. I was just really upset that we couldn't win the game for them."That was far from the only time that Kiffin addressed Brown's late touchdown, saying the play has literally kept him up every night since.
        
            
                Lane Kiffin created LSU's championship expectations. Now, he's struggling to live up to them
                
                    Chris Hummer                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Texas nightmareLSU fans have probably been thinking about that loss every second since the game ended, and it sounds like they have that in common with Kiffin. The first thing Kiffin brought up at the podium on Monday was the recurring nightmare he's had about losing to the Longhorns at the buzzer.
"I'll wake up literally every hour the last two nights, and I have this nightmare of the last play of the game," Kiffin said. "I think it's a nightmare every time I wake up that we didn't cover somebody to lose the game, and then we lost to Texas. I wake up, and it's real. Then I go back to sleep for an hour, and I wake up, and it's real again.'"Kiffin has also attempted to change history in his slumber.While explaining why he didn't call a timeout before Texas snapped the ball, Kiffin referenced his nightmare again. In it, he's trying to call timeout right before the Longhorns get the snap off."It happened so fast," Kiffin said. "I was asking, 'Do we want it?' I'm not placing any blame. They said, 'No, we're good.' That's why I was all the way down there because I was like, 'Hey, I got one if there's anything we don't like or the look. Let's use it.' I'm not placing any blame, but that's why I was down there.
"That's part of that nightmare. In it, I keep seeing myself call timeout."In reality, Kiffin kept that timeout in his pocket and quickly came to regret it. Despite all the attention given to how poorly the Tigers played their final defensive snap, the game was lost in key moments before that.Sam Leavitt's regressionComing up empty in three red-zone possessions is a great recipe for losing, and that's exactly what LSU did on Saturday night. Two of those possessions ended with a Sam Leavitt interception, and he totaled three interceptions throughout the game.Leavitt certainly earned his slice of the blame pie against Texas, and Kiffin acknowledged that his quarterback "made some really poor decisions" in the passing game. Kiffin even divulged that he spoke to Leavitt about taking care of the football in a tight game.
"He and I had talked Friday about how this game could be a defensive game," Kiffin said. " ... I knew their defense was really, really good. I talked to him about how it might be one of those games where I'll be conservative in some of my thinking, but he's got to take care of the ball if it's that type of game."Interestingly enough, Kiffin said Leavitt left some plays on the table late because the three interceptions made him more hesitant to pull the trigger."Then you get jammed up, and there are some plays in the fourth quarter where he's supposed to throw over here and make plays, but he's worried about throwing a fourth interception," Kiffin said. "He can kind of spiral on you."
If LSU is going to finish the 2026 season with a better taste in its mouth, Leavitt has to cut down on turnovers in high-leverage moments. That will start this weekend against a Tennessee defense that has made life difficult for opposing offenses, especially when they move into scoring range.

A win on Saturday night would get Oregon State to six wins and bowl-eligible, while Utah State needs a win to keep their hopes alive of making it to bowl season.
